subject: May maintenance window & rollback matrix — private VPC upgrade
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Proposed May maintenance window & compatibility matrix (private VPC)

Hi Andrew,

Following our call yesterday, attached is a proposed patch schedule and compatibility matrix for the Private VPC deployment in your EU cluster (sheet: node-by-node matrix). High-level asks:

- Maintenance window: Sat 29 May, 02:00–06:00 CEST (4h).
- Version pinning: runtime image inference-runtime:2.4.0 and model bundle tagged md-v20270511.
- Canary plan: 2 nodes (10% traffic) for first 20 minutes, then 50%/100%.
- Rollback trigger conditions: failed health checks >5% over 10m OR error-rate spike >3x baseline.

Attachments: priv-deploy-patch-matrix-2027-05.xlsx (matrix + timeline).

Before we lock the window I need your blackout constraints, and whether your team requires us to perform snapshots of the K/V cache and the DB before the patch. Also flag if Legal/security need a short summary for compliance (SOC2 evidence) — we can produce post-run logs.

Thanks,
Olga
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +44 20 7XX XXXX

From: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Proposed May maintenance window & compatibility matrix (private VPC)

Thanks Olga — Sat 29 May 02:00–06:00 CEST is workable for us, confirm tentative hold. A couple quick questions:

1) For rollback, do you plan a full cluster revert or node-level rollback? We prefer node-level that isolates rollback blast radius.
2) We need clarification on RPO/RTO expectations in your plan for DB schema changes. There shouldn’t be online DB schema migrations in this window; if required we need a separate change request.

Also, our Security team requires a short checklist showing artifact signing and the S3 object checksums for any runtime images you push. Can you include that in the playbook?

-Andrew
Andrew Miller
SRE Lead, Acme Corp
andy.miller@acme-corp.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:47:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Proposed May maintenance window & compatibility matrix (private VPC)

Andrew — thanks, good calls. Short answers:

- Rollback approach: node-level by default; we perform canary -> staggered node upgrade. If a rollback is triggered we will revert the affected nodes to the pinned image and route traffic away. Full cluster revert is an emergency-only path (longer RTO).
- DB schema: confirmed — no online schema migrations in this patch. If we need schema work we will schedule a separate CR with both teams.
- Artifact signing/checksums: included. I attached a concise rollback playbook (rollback-playbook-v1.2.pdf) with the checksum appendix (SHA256) and the signed image location.

Key excerpts from the playbook:
1) Pre-window prep (D-3): export KV snapshots, create DB backups (cold snapshot + WAL archive), capture node inventory and current image digests.
2) Execution (T0): shift 10% traffic to canary nodes, apply runtime update, run smoke tests (latency < 1.5x baseline, p95 < 700ms).
3) Rollback (if triggered): drain node, re-deploy pinned image, validate smoke tests, reintroduce to LB. Estimated rollback per node: 12–18 minutes.
4) Post-run artifacts: runbook will auto-upload run logs and SHA256 manifests to the audit bucket and generate a compliance artifact for your security team.

Please review the attached playbook and the matrix. Marcus — can you review the rollback timing and confirm the per-node rollback estimate aligns with the runtime instrumentation we have?

Olga

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:31:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Proposed May maintenance window & compatibility matrix (private VPC)

Looping in formal timings and a short rollback matrix. Notes: all internal commands below run from the operator bastion in the customer's VPC with the delegated service account (no root access).

Rollback matrix (condensed):
- Trigger: healthcheck-failures >5% for 10m OR error-rate >3x baseline => begin node rollback.
- Per-node rollback steps (est. duration):
  a) Drain LB (2–3m)
  b) Stop inference-runtime (1m)
  c) Re-deploy pinned image inference-runtime:2.4.0 (pull + cold start) (6–8m)
  d) Run smoke (5m)
  e) Gradually reintroduce to LB (2m)
- Total per-node RTO: 16–19 minutes.

We should also pin the model version via manifest (model: md-v20270511) and ensure model cache warmup uses the deterministic batch of profiled prompts — warmup approx 90s per replica.

Operational checklist (pre-window):
- D-3: verify image signatures & S3 checksums (Security).
- D-1: operator access verified, CI artifacts scanned (Lauren).
- T-15m: create snapshots + cgroups verification.

If everyone agrees I will add the exact CLI snippets to the playbook and the runbook automation will run the snapshot and upload the manifest to the audit bucket once completed. Lauren — please confirm the compliance attachment naming convention.

Marcus
VP, Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Proposed May maintenance window & compatibility matrix (private VPC)

Thanks Olga & Marcus — this addresses our concerns. We confirm the 29 May 02:00–06:00 CEST maintenance window. Our SREs will be on-call and will provide the blackout list by EOD Wed 26 May. I attached our internal change request with the requested fields (acme-change-request-513.docx).

One small ask: can you include in the playbook an explicit step that verifies the TLS cert chain after restart (internal load balancer certs sometimes rebind and break health checks) — we've seen this in an earlier rollout.

If Marcus can add the CLI snippets I will provide the SRE runbook and we can coordinate the dry-run on Wed 27 May (preferred).

Andrew
